cards.power: Discard a player's loyalty token to save yourself.
cards.lore: The institution doesn't love you back. It just manages you as a resource.
cards.gradeReason: Bureaucrat archetype clear but mechanic undercuts the embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: owl in brown suit trading loyalty chips. Mood: smug bureaucratic survival.

cards.power: Stall the game for 3 turns. Nobody gets to play.
cards.lore: Treason doesn't wear a mask; a cheap suit and denies your pension.
cards.gradeReason: Stalling mechanic with no character to inhabit — pure procedural drag.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir bureaucratic. Subject: mouse buried in paperwork at grey desk. Mood: suffocating institutional boredom.

cards.power: Force the player with the most points to lose half.
cards.lore: The apparatus always sacrifices its agents. The only question is when.
cards.gradeReason: Name alone triggers the scene — every spy at the table knows what to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda poster gone wrong. Subject: agent pushed into meat grinder by faceless handlers. Mood: cold institutional inevitability.

cards.power: Reveal a hidden objective card.
cards.lore: Espionage is 90% filing reports about lies you told to other liars.
cards.gradeReason: Raccoon with documents is perfect spy comedy — lore line is a mic drop.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: screwball noir. Subject: raccoon following trail of documents through corridors. Mood: bureaucratic absurdism.

cards.power: Ignore one attack, but you cannot draw cards next turn due to sheer apathy.
cards.lore: Too many missions, too many names. He runs out, but the door is walled over.
cards.gradeReason: Embody immediately — slumped posture, burnt-out badger, everyone gets it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: worn watercolor. Subject: battle-scarred badger at table, coffee untouched, staring at nothing. Mood: deep operational fatigue.

cards.power: Gain +2 strength, but auto-lose if a 'Truth' card is played.
cards.lore: Naïve idealism is the most dangerous form of espionage.
cards.gradeReason: Strong archetype but the auto-lose condition complicates the performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda poster satire. Subject: golden retriever soldier saluting burning flag. Mood: fervent belief before the collapse.

cards.power: Swap hands with an opponent, inheriting all their penalties.
cards.lore: He changed sides. Now nobody believes his story, least of all himself.
cards.gradeReason: Classic spy role — swap hands mechanic enacts defection perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cold War realism. Subject: ferret at border crossing, glancing over shoulder. Mood: irreversible threshold moment.

cards.power: Silence a player for one round.
cards.lore: The realization of sacrifice isn't a scream. It's absolute, hollow silence.
cards.gradeReason: Lore lands hard but the mechanic is abstract — needs context to fully embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: minimalist erasure. Subject: eraser removing a figure from a dossier. Mood: cold bureaucratic deletion.

cards.power: Copy another card's ability permanently, but discard your original name.
cards.lore: Live the role long enough, and the original identity dissolves entirely.
cards.gradeReason: Iconic — discarding your own name is the performance, not a metaphor.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: double exposure. Subject: frog in mirror seeing bulldog staring back. Mood: identity dissolution horror.

cards.power: Nullify an opponent's disguise.
cards.lore: What remains of a person after they've been used as a tool for a decade?
cards.gradeReason: Powerful question but the mechanic is purely reactive — no active performance hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychological realism. Subject: cracked mask revealing blurred animal face beneath. Mood: excavation of buried self.

cards.power: Force an opponent to play their next 3 turns with cards facing outward.
cards.lore: At some point, the fake loyalty becomes the only real thing left.
cards.gradeReason: Concept is devastating but forcing another player outward is control, not embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: body horror comedy. Subject: raccoon whose disguise fox mask has fused to face. Mood: identity trap with a grin.

cards.power: Play two conflicting action cards at once; take 2 damage to your own psyche.
cards.lore: Identity erosion isn't a side effect; it is the core mechanic of the system.
cards.gradeReason: Self-damage mechanic is bold but the double-card play is fiddly at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychological fracture. Subject: wolf with two screaming faces looking opposite directions. Mood: cognitive dissonance made flesh.

cards.power: Destroy an enemy card, but lose 2 health from the inevitable shrapnel.
cards.lore: Technology cannot replace psychology. Gadgets just make the body bags heavier.
cards.gradeReason: Spy comedy archetype lands but shrapnel blowback feels mechanically arbitrary.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: spy thriller slapstick. Subject: badger exploding oversized watch gadget in own face. Mood: tech hubris meets physical consequence.

cards.power: Look flashy, do exactly zero damage.
cards.lore: Glamour is a fantasy projection to hide the institutional trauma.
cards.gradeReason: Five words of power text — best card in the deck. Lore elevates it to masterclass.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: glamour noir. Subject: ferret in perfect tuxedo in front of explosion doing finger guns. Mood: devastating elegance over substance.

cards.power: Cancel a damage effect, but discard your entire hand in embarrassment.
cards.lore: A spy who makes no mistakes isn't a spy. It's boring corporate slop.
cards.gradeReason: Solid meta-comment on spy fiction tropes but the mechanic undercuts the charisma.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: superhero parody. Subject: cat in cape deflecting bullets while tripping over own cape. Mood: invulnerability myth exposed.

cards.power: Steal an opponent's turn by shouting "For the Country!"
cards.lore: "Patriot" isn't a character motivation; it's the lie they feed you at the door.
cards.gradeReason: You literally shout the mechanic aloud — performance and power fused perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: jingoistic poster satire. Subject: wolf in uniform pointing at sheep audience holding propaganda broadsheet. Mood: nationalism as con.

cards.power: Redirect an attack to a random third party.
cards.lore: Every information could be false. Every figure. Paranoia isn't a stylistic device. It is the baseline epistemic reality.
cards.gradeReason: The mechanic IS the concept — redirect and deny. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: geopolitical absurdism. Subject: duck waving multiple contradictory flags while explosion heads elsewhere. Mood: misdirection as statecraft.

cards.power: Rebound any Lore effect back at the caster.
cards.gradeReason: Pure reflective mechanic with no character or scene to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hall of mirrors. Subject: two foxes in identical suits facing each other across mirror. Mood: infinite mutual deception.

cards.power: Everyone must suddenly shuffle their active hands into the draw deck.
cards.lore: The audience no longer knows who to trust. The spy forgot years ago.
cards.gradeReason: Mass chaos mechanic enacts paranoia — everyone loses their footing simultaneously.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Escher-meets-spy-thriller. Subject: roulette wheel of agents pointing at each other. Mood: self-referential institutional madness.

cards.power: Peek at a card. If it's a Trap, you instantly lose.
cards.lore: Trust is just a currency waiting to be shorted.
cards.gradeReason: Arbitrary instant-lose mechanic — the risk is random, not performed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cold War thriller. Subject: hand reaching into glowing green folder labeled DANGER. Mood: information as weapon.

cards.power: Force an opponent to discard a card of their choice via intense politeness.
cards.lore: Spies never speak directly. The real information hides in the pauses and polite smiles.
cards.gradeReason: "Via intense politeness" is genius — slightly too subtle to trigger without context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Edwardian spy comedy. Subject: cats in suits having impossibly polite argument over fatal tea. Mood: lethality disguised as etiquette.

cards.power: Play a card face down; it triggers three turns from now.
cards.lore: A conversation where both know the other is lying, but courtesy demands silence. Politeness as a threat.
cards.gradeReason: Delayed trigger is clever but the table needs to track it — mechanic interrupts flow.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: diplomatic noir. Subject: speech bubble floating over fog-covered marsh, landing elsewhere. Mood: meaning deferred as tactical weapon.

cards.power: Give two opponents completely contradictory rules for the next turn.
cards.lore: Two bosses, two different directives for the same op. Navigate the verbal minefield.
cards.gradeReason: Working two masters is peak spy comedy — the contradiction IS the performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic chaos. Subject: squirrel on two phones receiving opposite orders. Mood: operational absurdism under deadline.

cards.power: Skip the current phase entirely.
cards.lore: True tradecraft is found in false self-corrections and strategic topic changes.
cards.gradeReason: Skip mechanic is elegant but passive — requires table sophistication to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hard-boiled interior. Subject: dog in fedora pausing mid-sentence, eyes moving sideways. Mood: silence as controlled detonation.

cards.power: Steal exactly 1 resource from the poorest player.
cards.lore: It starts with a minor compromise. Just a look away. Just one uncomfortable task.
cards.gradeReason: The quotation marks do everything — players immediately perform the self-justification.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: morality tale illustration. Subject: deer stealing single coin from sleeping mouse with pained expression. Mood: the first compromise.

cards.power: Destroy a friendly card to gain an immediate advantage.
cards.gradeReason: Sacrifice mechanic is clear but no specific scene or character to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: moral crossroads. Subject: badger pressing giant red BAD IDEA button with determined grimace. Mood: calculated self-corruption.

cards.power: Ignore a blatant rule violation this turn.
cards.lore: You don't leap into moral bankruptcy. You slide into it, one ignored atrocity at a time.
cards.gradeReason: Literally looking away while something happens — the table enacts moral compromise.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: institutional corruption. Subject: ostrich head in sand while chaos erupts around feet. Mood: willful unawareness as policy.

cards.power: Take control of the game board.
cards.lore: Only when you look back do you see the full, horrifying trajectory of your compromises.
cards.gradeReason: TAKE CONTROL OF THE GAME BOARD — four words, maximum performance, zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political cartoon maximalism. Subject: toad in three-piece suit lounging on game board like throne. Mood: corruption as comfortable furniture.

cards.power: Secretly leave a card under the table for someone else to find.
cards.lore: Character A knows X and acts like they don't. That's the engine of the genre.
cards.gradeReason: Physically enacted spy mechanic — brilliant in theory but needs the right table energy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cold War procedural. Subject: pigeon sliding envelope under park bench at midnight. Mood: information transfer as ritual.

cards.power: Hide your hand from all players for the rest of the game.
cards.lore: Character B knows Y and refuses to share it. Trust is just bad math.
cards.gradeReason: Defensive withholding — mechanic is practical, not performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surveillance noir. Subject: horse wearing blinders facing wall of screens showing everyone else. Mood: chosen ignorance.

cards.power: Reveal a secret rule only you and one other player know.
cards.lore: The audience knows more than the spy. It's a tragedy disguised as a thriller.
cards.gradeReason: Theatrical concept enacted at the table — the knowing glance between two players IS the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: theatrical aside. Subject: rabbit winking at audience while cop misses the point. Mood: tragedy wearing comedy's mask.

cards.power: Gain points for every card your opponents haven't played yet.
cards.lore: Secrets aren't facts; they are leverage.
cards.gradeReason: Passive scoring mechanic — the lore lands but the role is reactive, not performed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir strongroom. Subject: toad clutching locked chest while counting opponent's unplayed hands. Mood: information hoarding as power.

cards.power: Look at the top 3 cards of the deck and rearrange them.
cards.lore: Modern espionage tells the exact same story, just in server rooms instead of embassy parks.
cards.gradeReason: Deck manipulation is solid but the modern espionage reframe needs a beat to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tech noir. Subject: mouse navigating glowing server stacks with spy briefcase. Mood: Cold War updated to silicon.

cards.power: Reveal everyone's hidden cards; you lose your next turn and go into exile.
cards.lore: Knows the truth, speaks it, and pays the ultimate price. The public vs. The Apparatus.
cards.gradeReason: Complete narrative arc in one card — sacrifice the turn, reveal the truth, accept exile.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political martyrdom. Subject: pigeon releasing all documents from rooftop while agents below look up. Mood: truth as terminal act.

cards.power: Count the cards in an opponent's discard pile to perfectly guess their next move.
cards.lore: You aren't a person anymore. You are a profile, perfectly predicted.
cards.gradeReason: Counting discard piles is bookkeeping — powerful lore buried in dry mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: algorithmic surveillance. Subject: sheep reduced to spreadsheet columns with ID tag. Mood: personhood dissolved into data.

cards.power: Force a player to repeat their exact last action.
cards.lore: Cold, precise, democratic tracking. Anyone can be a spy. Everyone is a target.
cards.gradeReason: Compelling concept, but force-repeating an action is pure control with nothing to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surveillance realism. Subject: giant disembodied eye above city tracking single red dot. Mood: omniscient cold precision.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Drop a card randomly from your hand onto the table.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Espionage exacts a physical toll. You can't outrun the exhaustion of the body.
cards.gradeReason: Physical stress mechanic works but involuntary drop needs body language to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: physical disintegration. Subject: trembling gloved hand dropping dossier on marble floor. Mood: the body confessing what the mind denies.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): You cannot be targeted, but you also cannot attack or interact.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): The ultimate reward for a lifetime of service: dying completely alone.
cards.gradeReason: Defensive isolation mechanic — lore is devastating but card plays passively.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: institutional solitude. Subject: wolf alone in grey cell with single lamp, entire floor empty. Mood: safety as punishment.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Blank out the text of one opponent's card, making it useless.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Memory failure isn't a glitch; it's the brain trying to protect itself from the lies.
cards.gradeReason: Erasing an opponent's card text is clever but the embodiment of forgetting is elusive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic erasure. Subject: fox staring at blank ID card, own reflection fading. Mood: identity protection as identity loss.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Ignore all Lore effects for one round.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): The heart doesn't break; it just stops feeling anything at all to survive the frost.
cards.gradeReason: Shutdown mechanic — immune to lore but nothing to perform. Pure defensive positioning.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: emotional freeze-frame. Subject: heart encased in crystal ice block, still beating slowly. Mood: feeling suspended as survival strategy.

cards.power: Choose between losing your entire hand or losing half your health.
cards.lore: Loyalty to the machine vs. the desperate urge to survive. The machine usually wins.
cards.gradeReason: The forced impossible choice IS the performance — every player embodies it instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: scales of justice propaganda. Subject: ant facing giant boot of state apparatus on one side of scale. Mood: rigged game of survival.

cards.power: Discard a 'Good' alignment card to forcefully play an 'Evil' action.
cards.lore: What are you really fighting for, and what happens when you realize the cause is rotten?
cards.gradeReason: Alignment mechanic adds bookkeeping overhead to a powerful philosophical moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: moral crossroads realism. Subject: dog soldier discovering truth about mission orders. Mood: ideology collapsing against lived reality.

cards.power: Sacrifice a teammate's card to block a lethal attack aimed at you.
cards.lore: In an emergency, loyalty is the first thing jettisoned. Who sacrifices whom first?
cards.gradeReason: The spy's fundamental dilemma — sacrifice the teammate mechanic IS the performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: drowning allegory. Subject: two rats on sinking raft, one pushing the other off. Mood: survival overwriting loyalty.

cards.power: End the game immediately in a deeply unsatisfying draw.
cards.lore: To whom do you owe your loyalty when every single side is covered in filth?
cards.gradeReason: Ending in a draw is brilliant conceptually but deeply frustrating in practice.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: moral deadlock. Subject: signpost pointing six directions in fog, all labeled identically. Mood: paralysis as the only honest answer.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Predict the exact turn you will lose. If correct, you steal the win.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): You can't beat the system. You can only decide how it crushes you.
cards.gradeReason: The prediction mechanic is interesting but requires meta-game calculation, not roleplay.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: existential noir. Subject: hooded figure watching own chess defeat in reverse. Mood: fatalism as the only autonomy.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Obscure the board; no one can read card texts for one full turn.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): The aesthetic of doom. Action meets Detective meets existential despair.
cards.gradeReason: Atmospheric descriptor card — the lore describes a genre, not a performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir establishing shot. Subject: empty rainy alley, single lamppost, briefcase abandoned mid-frame. Mood: doom as atmosphere.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Take severe damage to deal double damage to an opponent.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Ethics under extreme conditions. There is no clean way out of the shadows.
cards.gradeReason: Self-sacrifice for double damage — the compromise IS the mechanic. Players feel it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: guilt-stained realism. Subject: hands with blood that won't wash off over pristine white surface. Mood: complicity made visible.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Lock one enemy card permanently. It cannot be moved or played.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Betrayal isn't a twist; it's the perfectly logical consequence of the game.
cards.gradeReason: Locking a card is strong control but the trap-setter doesn't perform — they obstruct.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: spider web procedural. Subject: single card trapped in web while game continues outside. Mood: entrapment as systemic logic.

cards.power: Broadcast your hand face-up to the table for +1 resource per turn.
cards.lore: Espionage is just an extreme mirror of our platform-driven, self-surveilled reality.
cards.gradeReason: You perform total self-exposure for points — surveillance capitalism enacted at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: social media dystopia. Subject: fox broadcasting selfie with all cards visible, audience applauding. Mood: radical transparency as product.

cards.power: Change the core rules of the game for one round.
cards.lore: Cognitive warfare and over-shared privacy. We built our own panopticon.
cards.gradeReason: Rule-changing is a GM power, not an embodied role — abstract authority without persona.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate surveillance architecture. Subject: lizard in hoodie rewiring game board infrastructure. Mood: platform power as invisible god.

cards.power: Sell an opponent's secret objective to the highest bidder.
cards.lore: Information is no longer just power. It is the only currency that matters.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic is pure transaction — good concept but nothing to inhabit or perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: slot machine noir. Subject: bandit machine with dossiers instead of fruit spinning. Mood: secrets commodified into randomness.

cards.power: Auto-counter an opponent based solely on their previous plays.
cards.lore: There is no 'private' self left. Just a string of exploitable data points.
cards.gradeReason: Chilling lore but the auto-counter mechanic is reactive — performance depends on opponent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: data surveillance realism. Subject: humanoid figure composed entirely of floating data tags. Mood: privacy abolished by accumulation.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Rip a dummy card in half (literally) to destroy two targets simultaneously.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): Deconstruct trust completely. Break the fourth wall and burn the pieces.
cards.gradeReason: Physical ripping is bold but requires a prop — logistically demanding at most tables.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: conceptual destruction. Subject: rabbit tearing page in half revealing nothing beneath the reality. Mood: epistemology as demolition.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Physically place this card over another to combine their texts.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): When the system is rigged, the only valid strategy is absolute Dadaist anarchy.
cards.gradeReason: Physical card combination is delightfully anarchic but technically fiddly mid-game.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dada collage. Subject: platypus duck-taping contradictory newspapers into new headline. Mood: anarchy as logical counter-system.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Ignore all rules. Draw a picture on the table. If people laugh, you survive.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): The truth is a joke, so you might as well be the one holding the punchline.
cards.gradeReason: Drawing on the table is great social mechanic but the laugh-test is subjectively judged.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: improv chaos. Subject: rabbit painting over NO TRESPASSING sign with giant grin. Mood: absurdism as survival strategy.

cards.power: POWER (Courier Prime): Win instantly if you can convince the table of a blatant, hilarious lie.
cards.lore: LORE (Courier Prime): We're all just animals playing a rigged game of epistemic collapse. Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Win by lying convincingly — the entire deck's thesis in one win condition. Perfect finale.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: epistemic chaos finale. Subject: fox at newsdesk delivering blatant nonsense to cheering animals. Mood: post-truth as punchline as truth.

verdict: Uncle FrizzleBob's sharpest institutional autopsy to date — spy fiction as operating system for modern life. The structural escalation from classic espionage archetypes through deception mechanics to surveillance capitalism critique is genuinely elegant. Weakness: the Courier Prime counter-mechanic section (pages 11-15) leans too mechanical and loses the performative edge of earlier cards. Named strength: The Hollow Tuxedo and The Voluntary Spy may be two of the finest single cards in the entire corpus. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: For anyone who's been betrayed by an institution, worked for two bosses, or shouted 'For the Country!' with a straight face — 56 spy-wrestling cards that make Cold War psychology a contact sport.

coverQA.coverNote: Cover is firing on all cylinders — the FrizzleBob rabbit spy energy reads from across the room. 'What the FLUFF?!' annotation is precisely the right level of self-aware absurdism. If this doesn't get clicked on Gumroad, nothing will.

notes: Cards organized in 5 thematic clusters: (1) Classic spy archetypes pages 2-5 warm illustrated style, (2) Deception mechanics pages 6-8, (3) Information warfare pages 9-10 KayfaBINGO watermark variant, (4) Psychological cost Courier Prime section page 11, (5) Systemic/epistemic critique pages 12-15 bolder title typography. Corner annotations (SHHH!, HIDDEN!, KALAM, WINK!, BOOM! etc.) serve as performance cues not RAF dice boxes — RAF=false confirmed. Pages 4 and 12-15 use larger all-caps display titles distinguishing them as a second act. The surveillance capitalism cluster (The Voluntary Spy, The Platform Architect, The Monetized Secret, The Profile) is a standout contemporary addition. THE DOUBLE MIRROR and THE NECESSARY EVIL lore text was not legible in PDF renders — marked null. THE ABSURD TRUTH 'Stay fluffy!' sign-off is the perfect deck closer.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: SECRET SPY SUPLEXES – The Tradecraft You Already Run, Dealt Face-Up (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

You have worked for two bosses who wanted opposite things. You have shouted something patriotic to win an argument you already knew was rigged. You have built a clean face for the feed and called it being honest. Congratulations, agent. You have been running tradecraft for years.

Spy fiction handed you the tuxedo and the exploding watch and let you believe the spy was someone else, somewhere colder, holding a licence you will never get. Take the costume off and the job description is depressingly familiar. Manage a face. Hold a secret as leverage. Broadcast your whole hand for a little applause and call it sharing. The Cold War did not end. It got a platform, a profile, and a notification badge, and it moved into your pocket. Secret Spy Suplexes deals that out as fifty-six moves and dares you to perform each one with a straight face.

This is Social Story Wrestling for the surveillance age. You pick up a card, you play the agent, and the table decides whether your cover holds or comes apart mid-sentence. No clearance, no dossier to memorise, just the oldest game there is: lie well enough, and the room signs off.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Secret Spy Suplexes Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Hollow Tuxedo, the agent who looks flashy and does exactly zero damage, The Voluntary Spy, who broadcasts their entire hand for points, and The Patriotic Lie, which steals a turn the second you shout "For the Country!"
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no security clearance, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one law that every card can claim anything, right up until the table refuses to buy the pitch.
- The Five-Act Burn: the deck escalates on purpose, from the classic Cold War archetypes like Institutional Betrayal, The Sleeper Agent, and The Defector, through deception and information warfare, into the section nobody sees coming, where the surveillance state turns out to be you, willingly, every morning, for free.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
You are not buying a static PDF. You are buying into the cover-up cycle. Every future chapter, every sibling deck that follows the same thread of who is watching whom and who is paying for the privilege, lands in your library as a free update. The file keeps recruiting.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I make these because the surest way to survive a rigged game is to learn its moves with your own hands, out loud, where everyone can watch you do it. Are you broke? Enter "0" and take it. Run the moves. Catch yourself running them for real. Want to support the craft? Every coin goes straight into the next deck and the next round of cards.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"Everyone at the table is lying. The winner is just the one you agreed to believe."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
